definitions.explanation: The act of entering a restricted or prohibited area. Most commonly seen in prohibition signs and warnings.

examples.japanese: {工事中|こうじちゅう}のため、{立|た}ち{入|い}りはご{遠慮|えんりょ}ください。
examples.english: Please refrain from entering, as construction is underway.

examples.japanese: {無断|むだん}{立|た}ち{入|い}りは{法律|ほうりつ}で{罰|ばっ}せられることがある。
examples.english: Unauthorized entry may be punishable by law.

notes:
{立|た}ち{入|い}り means entering an area, especially one that is restricted. Most commonly encountered as part of prohibition signs.

FORMS:
The verb is {立|た}ち{入|い}る (to enter, to trespass). This noun form is the masu-stem nominalization.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立|た}ち{入|い}り{禁止|きんし}: no entry, keep out (the most common phrase)
- {立|た}ち{入|い}り{検査|けんさ}: on-site inspection (by authorities)
- {立|た}ち{入|い}り{調査|ちょうさ}: on-site investigation
- {無断|むだん}{立|た}ち{入|い}り: unauthorized entry
- {立|た}ち{入|い}り{制限|せいげん}: entry restrictions

USAGE:
Almost always used in formal, official, or legal contexts. You will see {立|た}ち{入|い}り{禁止|きんし} on signs at construction sites, private property, and restricted areas. In everyday conversation, {入|はい}る is the normal word for entering.
